scenes.text: Most interfaces are cut for “users aged twenty-five to thirty-four.” Nobody in that bracket has taste. A person does.
Baste starts with one person: the films they rewatch, the music they work to, the rooms they feel at home in, and the things they can’t stand in an app.

scenes.scene: The same screen re-cut for Moss, Ren and Ada
scenes.text: Then it fits an interface to them. Same screen, three people. The layout, the type, the colour and the motion all change.

scenes.scene: The archive filling with real candidates
scenes.text: To find a direction, Baste tries dozens of loose versions, warm and cool, sparse and dense, and a vision judge looks at every one.
It keeps the best in each region, not one winner. So you see the real range of options before anything is final.

scenes.scene: Finished suite: hero, icons, loop, tokens
scenes.text: What comes out is ready to use: images, vector icons, ambient loops, and design tokens for CSS, Tailwind or Panda.
And you can ask the persona why. They’ll tell you, in their own words, what they love and what would make a design feel like theirs.
Bring your own people. Measure them in the Studio, and cut something that fits.
